papers.result: Section2.2 defines signed incidence, opposite-incidence walks and connected balanced Euler tours (Lemma1). Section5 reduces cyclic Chinese postman to minimum-cost bidirected flow and interprets it for a prescribed k-molecule spectrum. These directly precede the candidate's graph traversal interpretation. Their spectrum-constrained cyclic model is not the candidate's arbitrary-length linear superstring problem. No novelty is claimed for half-Euler or bidirected representation. Do not silently import their exact optimization theorem as a theorem for the candidate's input model. Sections3-4 explicitly distinguish selected-edge assembly and required-subwalk assembly from spectrum-only CPP: they prove NP-hardness via split vertices and separator-letter cycles respectively. Consequently, the polynomial spectrum assembly theorem cannot silently stand in for an arbitrary set of read requirements.

papers.result: Their involution is fixed-point-free on both vertices and arcs. Regular paths avoid mate arc pairs; symmetric integer flows decompose into paired paths/cycles, with an associated parity corollary. The bidirected correspondence chooses one representative per vertex pair. RCS128 permits fixed vertices including epsilon, so this is antecedent context, not a verbatim theorem application without a reduction. The candidate's fixed-vertex parity and elementary traversal argument remain explicit, and half-Euler earns no contribution credit. Section5 also supplies a concrete two-cycle splicing antecedent: two self-symmetric cycles meeting at x and its mate are recombined from their two complementary paths into an exchanged pair. Thus cutting two invariant cycles at two common points and exchanging halves is not in itself a new operation. RCS128 uses individually reflection-fixed staircase profiles and fixed-axis endpoints, and its potential residual is compatibility with ordered profiles, an unchanged left anchor, batch reflection/reclassification and the source host budget. This comparison must be passed to the contribution gate rather than silently preserving broad credit for splicing.
